_about: Inputs of the GM's Boeing balance-sheet tracker (finance.py) for Control's objective 'repair the balance sheet: debt back to historical levels'. Debt is NET debt (total debt minus cash and short-term investments), the measure both broker models and the S&P Capital IQ consensus forecast on a consistent basis. Money in $B, constant 2026 dollars (nominal figures deflated at the engine board's 2.2% CPI). Objective scoring only: the board's ΔPV and its own debt penalty on $45B of gross debt are unchanged.

sources.start: End-2026E net debt $22.53B: S&P Capital IQ consensus mean (TheBoeingCompanyNYSEBAEstimatesReport.xls, Consensus 'Net Debt', 5 estimates); GS $22.55B (GoldmanSachs_BA72826_Jul_30_2026.xlsx BS row 64), MS $23.01B (341995.BA.N.XLSM Balance_Sheet_Annual 'Net Debt'). Gross debt at 2Q26A $45.9B (both models), the board's $45B.
sources.base_fcf: Free cash flow 2027E-2030E, S&P Capital IQ consensus mean (Consensus 'Free Cash Flow'): $5.67B, $9.86B, $13.03B, $15.04B nominal (14, 15, 10 and 3 estimates). MS: 6.20, 10.33, 10.84, 12.76; GS: 6.51, 10.54, 13.64, 16.65. Held flat in real terms after 2030 (no broker forecast beyond 2030-31). None of these includes a new airplane programme.
sources.historical: Net debt 2010A-2018A (GS BS row 64, one definition throughout): 1.90, 1.10, -3.15, -5.62, -4.02, -2.09, -0.08, 1.13, 5.28; mean -$0.62B (a small net cash). Gross debt averaged $11.0B (range $9.1-13.8B).
sources.validation: With base cash flow only, the tracker gives net debt $16.98B at end-2027 and $7.54B at end-2028 against consensus $16.94B and $7.21B, and reaches zero in 2029 (MS has -$3.6B in 2029E).
sources.capital_allocation: Debt first: every dollar of free cash flow goes to net debt until it is back at the historical level; after that surplus cash goes to the owners. MS models no buybacks to 2030 (net cash $16.2B in 2030E); GS models $42B of buybacks in 2027E-2030E (net debt $17.4B in 2030E). Boeing's Board reserves shareholder returns for itself until the rating is solid.
sources.stress: Stress case: base free cash flow one-third below consensus in every year. The lowest 2027E-2030E estimates are 79-92% of the mean (4.50, 7.99, 11.93, 13.34), but Boeing's record is worse: consensus 2026 free cash flow was cut from $5.05B to $2.15B (-57%) in twelve months (Trends sheet), and 2019-2025 free cash flow was negative in five of seven years.

historical_label: its 2010-2018 average of about -$0.6B, a small net cash
method_short: Net debt is total debt minus cash and short-term investments. It starts at the consensus end-2026 figure ($22.5B) and falls by free cash flow: the analysts' consensus to 2030 (held flat after), plus 79% of the profit the game adds or takes away against its baseline, less programme cash as it is spent (each bill over its development years on your CFO's planning curve, not at EIS as the board books it), less 3% real interest on any debt the game adds. Debt comes first; once net debt is back at the historical level, surplus cash goes to the owners. The stress case runs the same path with base free cash flow one-third lower.
